format: Edited sequence of real browser captures; hard cuts and reading holds; no continuous screen recording, audio, fabricated cursor, live model or real-time timing claim
assistance: Captured, edited and verified with OpenAI Codex assistance

steps.title: Welcome to AeroTest Copilot
steps.caption:
Explore a fictional research-aircraft subsystem.
This is an edited sequence of real browser captures, with reading time added.

steps.title: Choose a repeatable scenario
steps.caption:
Select Sensor disagreement, seed 42 and 30000 ms.
The simulator uses fixed 100 ms ticks; the seed repeats the evidence.

steps.title: Run the C++ simulator and save evidence
steps.caption:
The run completes with 904 records and its own execution ID.
DEGRADED before shutdown describes subsystem state, not a test verdict.

steps.title: Read scoped requirement checks
steps.caption:
The disagreement response and transition policy pass their observed checks.
Unexercised checks remain INCONCLUSIVE; AT-REQ-004 and 005 are unassessed.

steps.title: Request a scripted explanation
steps.caption:
Select AT-REQ-001 and explain the saved checks.
The response uses build_report and resolve_citations; no live model is called.

steps.title: Open an original citation
steps.caption:
One of 13 citations resolves to sensor A at 2000 ms: 20043 mdegC.
The original event ID, timestamp, unit and acquisition details stay visible.

steps.title: Compare the recorded sensor samples
steps.caption:
Sensor B is biased from 2000 through 3900 ms.
The chart uses recorded delivery times and explicit units, without interpolation.

steps.title: Inspect the response transition
steps.caption:
Record 77 shows NOMINAL to DEGRADED at 2500 ms; shutdown occurs at 30000 ms.
These are scoped observations in an educational simulation, not a compliance verdict.
